title: The Teacher Who Drew the Flag

pages.text: On the Friday before Independence Day, Ato and Ofosua painted a large flag on a sheet of paper. Ofosua did the red stripe, Ato did the green, and they argued about the gold. “Where does the star go?” asked Ato. “In the middle,” said Ofosua. “Black, and with five points.” Mr Bortey came over to look.

“Where does the star go?” asked Ato.
“In the middle,” said Ofosua.
“Black, and with five points.” Mr Bortey came over to look.
pages.alt: Two children paint a large flag on paper in a bright classroom.

pages.text: “Do you know who first drew the flag you are painting?” asked Mr Bortey. “A teacher and artist named Theodosia Okoh designed it in 1957,” he said. “She was the one who put the stripes and the star together. A flag is a picture that a whole country agrees to share, and a teacher helped make it.”

“A teacher and artist named Theodosia Okoh designed it in 1957,” he said.
“She was the one who put the stripes and the star together.
A flag is a picture that a whole country agrees to share, and a teacher helped make it.”
pages.alt: A woman at a desk draws stripes of red, gold and green on a large sheet.

pages.text: “Look at the colours,” said Mr Bortey. “People often say red stands for the blood of those who died for the country’s freedom. Gold stands for the mineral wealth of the land, such as gold and diamonds. Green stands for the forests and farms. These are the most widely told meanings, but you may hear other readings too.”

Gold stands for the mineral wealth of the land, such as gold and diamonds.
Green stands for the forests and farms.
These are the most widely told meanings, but you may hear other readings too.”
pages.alt: A flag with three stripes and small pictures of a farm, a mine and a crowd of people.

pages.text: “And the black star?” asked Ofosua. “The black star stands for the freedom of Africa and for unity against colonial rule,” said Mr Bortey. “It is linked to the Black Star Line, a shipping company started by a man named Marcus Garvey. That is also why our national football team is called the Black Stars.” Ato whispered, “So the football team and the flag share a star.”

That is also why our national football team is called the Black Stars.” Ato whispered, “So the football team and the flag share a star.”
pages.alt: A black star over a ship and a football team wearing black stars on their shirts.

pages.text: “The flag was first raised on 6 March 1957,” said Mr Bortey. “That was the day the Gold Coast became Ghana, a free country, with Kwame Nkrumah as its leader. People call Ghana the first country in sub-Saharan Africa to win independence from European colonial rule. We chose the name Ghana from an older empire, as we learned in our lesson last term.”

We chose the name Ghana from an older empire, as we learned in our lesson last term.”
pages.alt: A crowd waves flags at a ceremony as a flag is raised.

pages.text: “There is one more twist,” said Mr Bortey. “For a few years in the 1960s the flag was changed. Gold was replaced with white. After Nkrumah left power in 1966, the original design came back. Books do not agree on every date, so we say: in the 1960s, then restored.” Ofosua laughed. “Even flags have their stories.”

pages.alt: Two flags side by side, one with gold and one with white in the middle stripe.

pages.text: “Why does a flag matter?” asked Ato. “It is a symbol,” said Mr Bortey. “It is not only cloth. When people stand under it, they remember that they belong together, and that others fought, spoke, wrote and taught so that they could. We do not worship a flag. We honour what it stands for.”

When people stand under it, they remember that they belong together, and that others fought, spoke, wrote and taught so that they could.
We do not worship a flag.
We honour what it stands for.”
pages.alt: Children stand in a line before a flagpole as the teacher speaks quietly.

pages.text: On Monday, the whole school stood in the yard. As the flag went up, Ato counted on his fingers. “2026 take away 1957 is 69 years,” he whispered. “Sixty-nine,” said Ofosua. “And a teacher helped begin it.” Mr Bortey smiled and nodded. When the anthem ended, the two friends held their painted flag high. The end.

From the colour of the pitch

items: The flag was first raised on 6 March 1957.
The flag was changed for a few years in the 1960s.
The original design was restored after 1966.
